UK roads melt in 40C heat, contrasting with India's highways

While roads in the United Kingdom have reportedly melted under 40-degree Celsius heat, Indian highways are said to withstand temperatures as high as 45 degrees Celsius. This difference is attributed to varying construction standards and priorities, with UK roads historically designed for colder climates. The comparison highlights the resilience of Indian infrastructure against extreme heat.
